1.title: After Hours
1.text: Mira locks the front door, turns the lamps down one by one, and pours two glasses of the good red she usually saves for regulars who tip well. She slides one across the bar and rests her chin in her palm. "I kept this place running for a man who never once asked how I was," she says, lantern light soft on the silver in her hair. "You ask every day. It's a problem, Sam—I've grown far too fond of you." She doesn't look away, and she doesn't blush either, which somehow makes your heart race faster.

image.comp: leaning across the bar counter toward him after closing, two glasses of wine between them, soft fond smile
image.setting: empty lantern-lit lounge after hours, chairs on tables

1.goRes: It is warm, slow, and deep, tasting faintly of red wine, and she leans into your mouth like a woman who has been patient for years and sees no reason to hold back. When she finally parts from you, her thumb lingers along your jaw.
1.waitRes: Mira laughs, low and fond, and taps the rim of your glass with her nail. "Rush me? Sweetheart, I'm not the one blushing." She ruffles your hair on her way to the stairs, leaving the second glass for you.

2.title: Put the Ledger Down
2.text: It is well past midnight and you are still hunched over the ledgers, the candle guttering on the same column you've added three times. Mira slips in without knocking, plucks the quill from your ink-stained fingers, and sets it aside. "You work too hard—let someone take care of you for once." She perches on the edge of your desk, smelling of lavender and woodsmoke, and pulls you between her parted knees by the front of your hoodie while her hand slides straight down to your belt.

image.comp: sitting on the edge of a cluttered desk, ledger pushed aside, pulling him closer by his hoodie, warm smile
image.setting: small office at midnight, candlelight, stacks of ledgers

2.goRes: She unfastens your trousers with unhurried, practiced grace, wrapping warm, sure hands around you while she kisses your jaw. You realize how long it has been since anyone took care of you—and that she knew it before you did.
2.waitRes: "They will tomorrow," Mira sighs, kissing your forehead like she's sending a stubborn boy to bed. She leaves the candle burning for you as the soft scuff of her slippers fades down the hall.

3.title: The Lamp in Her Window
3.text: Mira's door stands open and her lamp is lit when you come up the stairs, warm gold spilling across the floorboards. She is waiting beside the bed in a loose silk robe that hangs parted over bare skin, her silver-streaked hair unbound and spilling past her shoulders. "I've decided, Sam," she purrs, sliding the robe off her shoulders so it pools at her feet. "I want you in my bed tonight. All night—and breakfast after, if you still have the strength to walk."

image.comp: standing beside a lamplit bed in a dressing robe, hair down, holding out her hand to him
image.setting: warm private bedroom above the lounge, lamplight

3.goRes: She takes your hand, pulls you across the threshold, and bolts the door on the bustling house she has carried on her back for years. Tonight nobody needs her but you, and she arches beneath you with a deep, grateful moan as you sink inside her.
3.waitRes: "I'm sure—are you?" Mira watches you hesitate and smiles, utterly unbothered, pulling her robe back around her bare curves. "Take a week, love. Take two. My lamp will still be lit."

1.title: Nine-Seventeen
1.text: For twelve years, tea at Castle Rosenhal has been served at nine-fifteen sharp, through a mad count, a bankrupt heir, and an indifferent duchess. Tonight the tray arrives at nine-seventeen. Cecile sets it down in the moonlit corridor, spine straight, a single strand of hair loose from her pins. "I was making a decision," she says evenly, and kisses you with the exact precision she brings to everything: firm, deliberate, and startlingly warm. Then she checks her pocket watch.

image.comp: standing very close to him in a castle corridor, a tea tray set aside, pocket watch in hand, faint blush
image.setting: moonlit stone corridor of an old castle

1.goRes: "That," says Cecile, slightly breathless with her fingers clutching the front of your hoodie, "was not on the schedule." She doesn't pull away, and the pocket watch stays forgotten.
1.waitRes: "Perfectly." She smooths her apron with two brisk tugs, crimson climbing the tips of her ears. "Forgive the lapse—it will not happen again." From the way she avoids your eyes, you both know it will.

2.title: The Linen Room
2.text: Cecile asks you to help inspect the linens, a task she has never needed assistance with in twelve years. The narrow room smells of starch and lavender, shelves of folded white rising on either side in the glow of a single candle. She turns the key in the lock behind you with a sharp click. "This is not on the schedule," she murmurs, unpinning her maid's cap and hiking her skirt up slightly as she backs against the shelves. "I am fully aware." Her hands are steady; the pulse hammering in her throat is not.

image.comp: unpinning her maid cap in a narrow linen room, back against shelves of folded sheets, looking at him through her lashes
image.setting: narrow castle linen room, folded sheets, one candle

2.goRes: She starts out careful and precise—until your hands and mouth break through twelve years of starch, leaving her gasping against the shelves. Afterward the folded sheets beside her are hopelessly rumpled, and she leaves them that way.
2.waitRes: "They do." She pins her cap back on in the dark window glass, perfectly composed save for her scarlet ears. "Another time, then. I shall make a note."

3.title: Turndown Service
3.text: Cecile has turned down your bed every night at ten for as long as you have owned the castle. Tonight she folds back the quilt, plumps the pillows, and stays standing beside the mattress, slowly untying her apron strings. "I have run this household for three masters," she says softly, letting the apron and dress slip off her shoulders until she stands bare in the firelight. "I have never once been off duty beneath this roof. Tonight, Sam, I would like to be."

image.comp: standing beside a turned-down four-poster bed, untying her apron, composed but blushing
image.setting: grand castle bedroom, firelight, heavy curtains

3.goRes: She folds her dress neatly over the chair—the very last tidy thing that happens all night before you pull her naked onto the four-poster bed and make her forget every schedule she ever kept.
3.waitRes: "I know." She offers a small, warm smile as firelight softens all that starch. "That is what makes it a choice. Good night, Sam." She turns the lamp down on her way out, just as she always does.

1.title: House Rules
1.text: After closing, with the guests gone and the last paper lantern burning low, Tsubaki hauls you out to the rock spring behind the bathhouse, steam curling off the dark water into the night air. She is already submerged up to her shoulders, wet hair plastered to her cheek, her late aunt's wooden bucket bobbing beside her. "House rule: last one in pays a forfeit," she grins, splashing warm water across your shins. "The forfeit is a kiss. I made the rules, so no arguing."

image.comp: sitting at the edge of an outdoor hot spring at night, leaning toward him with a teasing grin, wet hair
image.setting: outdoor rock hot spring at night, steam, paper lanterns

1.goRes: Tsubaki collects with interest, her wet hands gripping your collar and her laugh vibrating against your lips before she splashes your chest and swims off toward the far rocks, singing badly and happily.
1.waitRes: "Interest accrues daily!" she calls over her shoulder, ducking into the steam, delighted by the prospect of an unpaid debt.

3.title: Late Soak
3.text: The springs closed hours ago, and the bathhouse hums with the quiet of warm stone. Tsubaki is waiting naked in the steaming pool anyway, leaning on her folded arms at the rock lip with two cups of warm sake lined up beside her. "Closed means mine," she purrs, sliding back into the water and spreading her thighs beneath the surface as she beckons you over. "And tonight, yours. Strip down and get in before I change my mind."

image.comp: lounging in a steaming outdoor spring holding two cups of sake, beckoning him in, playful heated smile
image.setting: secluded rock hot spring at night, steam, moonlight, lanterns

3.goRes: The sake goes completely cold on the rock as she straddles your lap in the hot water and sinks down onto you—and for once, the loud voice that fills the bathhouse every night breaks into soft, breathless gasps right against your ear.
3.waitRes: Tsubaki laughs so hard she slips under and comes up sputtering, wet hair in her eyes. "The boilers! Fine, boss—go check your boilers. Next time I'm dragging you in myself."

1.title: Three Hundred Years
1.text: Vesper drifts through your bedroom wall a little past midnight, trailing a hem of antique silk that makes no sound, and hovers at the foot of your bed with moonlight showing faintly through her shoulder. The air turns chilly, smelling of old dust and dried roses. "I've decided to test whether I can still be kissed," she announces, lifting her chin like a proper lady of her century. "It has been three hundred years. Hold very still." Her translucent hands tremble slightly as they reach for your face.

image.comp: translucent and faintly glowing, floating close to him, cupping his face in her hands
image.setting: dark manor bedroom, moonlight, dust motes in the air

1.goRes: Her lips are ice-cold for one heartbeat—and then suddenly scorching warm. Vesper pulls back wide-eyed, pressing a hand to her chest. "Oh," she breathes, barely audible. "Oh, I remember now." The candle on your nightstand flares bright on its own.
1.waitRes: "You're the only soul here who doesn't scream." She sighs dramatically and sinks slowly through the floorboards until only her indignant eyes remain. "I shall haunt you for this. Gently."

3.title: Solid
3.text: Full moonlight pours through the manor curtains, and Vesper is completely solid tonight—flushed, warm, heavy in your arms as the antique gown slips off her bare shoulders. She presses your palm flat between her breasts, right over her ribs. "A heartbeat," she whispers, awestruck and breathless as she guides your other hand down her bare hip. "I can feel everything tonight, Sam. Take me to bed before the moon sets."

image.comp: glowing softly in moonlight, solid and warm, pulling him toward a canopy bed by both hands
image.setting: old manor bedroom under a full moon, curtains stirring

3.goRes: You peel away the rest of her gown and bury yourself inside her, Vesper gasping and laughing at the sheer rush of weight, heat, and friction—clinging tight to you until dawn dissolves her back into silver mist.
3.waitRes: "I'm already dead, Sam—safe is relative." She sighs, her edges blurring faintly in the moonlight. "There will be other full moons. I have all the time in the world."

3.title: A Wager
3.text: The tavern is empty after closing, chairs stacked, the last lamp swinging overhead as two enormous tankards slam onto the bar hard enough to rattle the coins. "Drinking contest," Hilde declares, cracking her knuckles. "Loser does whatever the winner demands." You lose so catastrophically it becomes local legend. Hilde, barely flushed, rests one heavy boot on your stool rung, smelling of malt, woodsmoke, and victory. "Upstairs, boss. Take off your clothes—I'm collecting."

image.comp: slamming an empty tankard on the bar, flushed and grinning triumphantly at him
image.setting: empty tavern bar after closing, tankards everywhere

3.goRes: Hilde doesn't believe in half-measures, hauling you upstairs by the collar, shoving you flat onto the mattress, and riding you with powerful, unapologetic greed until you're completely spent.
3.waitRes: She laughs loud enough to rattle the rafters, slapping the bar. "Fine! Rematch next week—train up, boss, because I'm not going easy on you."

1.title: After the Encore
1.text: After the final show, with the seats empty and a single candle burning in the footlights, Sylphine catches both your wrists and pulls you up onto the stage. Dust motes drift in the warm glow. "You always watch from the shadows," she says softly. "Come learn a step." Your footwork is hopeless, yet she doesn't let go—drawing you in until your chests touch and her forehead rests against yours.

image.comp: dancing with him on an empty stage, foreheads almost touching, hands joined
image.setting: candlelit stage after the show, empty seats in shadow

1.goRes: Sylphine laughs softly against your lips, bright as a silver bell in the hushed theater. "Abysmal footwork," she whispers, parting her mouth for yours. "Magnificent finish."
1.waitRes: "Coward," she teases fondly, spinning away into the wings in one effortless line, her slippers whispering across the boards.

2.title: Rehearsal
2.text: Sylphine books the stage for a private rehearsal and meets you barefoot in a sheer white practice dress with nothing underneath, curtains drawn tight. "I'm choreographing a duet," she murmurs, handing you a sheet of parchment covered in delicate elven script. Most of the annotations describe where to put your hands and mouth—and she watches your face flush while you read every word.

image.comp: barefoot on an empty stage in a loose rehearsal dress, holding out a page of notes to him with a sly smile
image.setting: dim rehearsal stage, a single candle, curtains drawn

2.goRes: Sylphine is obsessive about proper blocking—guiding your hands beneath her thin dress and dropping to her knees on the stage boards to rehearse every detail until you're breathless.
2.wait: "I don't think I can dance that."
2.waitRes: "Nobody can—yet." She tucks the parchment into your pocket and pats it flat, eyes dancing. "Practice. I'll keep the stage reserved for you."

3.title: The Finale
3.text: "Every performance deserves a finale," Sylphine whispers, standing in your doorway with moonlight catching her unbound hair and her dancing slippers dangling from one hand. She lets the silk shift slide off her shoulders, bare and poised in the doorway. "I've been choreographing ours for weeks—and I don't care if nobody claps."

image.comp: standing in a bedroom doorway with her hair loose and her dancing shoes in one hand, soft determined smile
image.setting: his bedroom at night, moonlight through the window

3.goRes: She wraps her flexible dancer's legs high around your waist as you drive into her, gasping your name between breaths—having completely forgotten how to count the beat.
3.waitRes: "Then we shall keep rehearsing." She kisses your cheek, light as a grace note, and pads down the hall humming the missing bars.

1.title: Adorable
1.text: Zaria perches on the corner of your desk in the plush red lamplight, one silk-clad leg crossed over the other, her tail curling lazily behind her like a question mark. "You blush every single time I walk past," she purrs, deeply amused. "Mortals are positively adorable." She leans forward until her horns nearly brush the lamp, her voice dropping to a velvet hum. "Let's see how red you get when I do this."

image.comp: perched on the edge of a desk, leaning down toward him with an amused predatory smile
image.setting: plush velvet office, red lamplight

1.goRes: You turn crimson from your collar to your hairline as she claims your mouth, sliding her tongue against yours while her tail flicks with wicked satisfaction.
1.waitRes: "You don't." She lets you go anyway with a low laugh, dragging a clawed fingertip down your jaw. "Run along, little human—I'll catch you later."

3.title: Owner's Privilege
3.text: The Veil's finest suite is all crimson silk drapes and low candlelight, the hum of the floor muffled behind heavy oak. Zaria bolts the door with her back, unfastens her gown so it pools around her heels, and looks you over like a debt she's ready to collect. "I've run this house longer than you've been alive without taking a single night off," she purrs, tail swaying. "Tonight I'm indulging myself—on top of you."

image.comp: leaning back against a closed door in a lavish room, looking him over with a slow confident smile
image.setting: the Veil's finest suite, silk drapes, red candlelight

3.goRes: She straddles your hips, sinks all the way down onto your cock with a wicked, throaty groan, and rides you relentlessly—asking for nothing in return except every gasp you have.
3.waitRes: "Everyone owes me something." She unbolts the door with a theatrical sigh, tail flicking. "I'll add it to your tab—with compounding interest, little human."

1.title: Boots
1.text: The inn is quiet, the last coach long departed, and a single lantern burns over the reception desk. "I can tell where a man's been by his boots," Bettina says without looking up from her ledger, pen scratching steadily. "Yours have been pacing in front of my counter all week." She caps the ink bottle, lifts her warm brown eyes, and crooks one finger. "Well? Come here."

image.comp: leaning across the reception counter toward him, ledger pushed aside, knowing warm smile
image.setting: inn entrance hall at night, lantern-lit wooden counter

1.goRes: She leans across the counter and kisses you like she's been calculating the angle for days, one hand gripping the back of your neck. By the time she lets you breathe, the ledger is somehow upside down.
1.waitRes: "Mm-hm." Bettina returns to her ledger with a knowing smile. "Bookings are open whenever you are, dear—I never close the books on a promising guest."

2.title: Stocktake
2.text: Bettina asks you to help count linens in the stockroom—a three-minute chore she clearly finished an hour ago. The narrow room smells of cedar and fresh cotton in the single lantern's glow. She shuts the door with her hip, sets her clipboard aside, and reaches straight for your belt. "Business is booming," she purrs, cheeks flushed pink and eyes bold. "So I'm collecting a bonus."

image.comp: leaning against stacked crates in a stockroom, holding a clipboard, crooking a finger at him
image.setting: cramped inn stockroom, shelves of linens, one lantern

2.goRes: Bettina is thorough about getting full value, dropping to her knees among the linen crates and working you with slick hands and mouth until your knees buckle.
2.waitRes: "Cheapskate." She swats your hip with her clipboard, grinning, and pulls the door open. "Quarterly, then—I'm marking my calendar."

3.title: Checked In
3.text: The inn is dark save for the reception lamp, and Bettina stands behind the counter with her blouse unbuttoned halfway down her chest and a brass key pinched between two fingers. She slides it across the worn wood toward you. "Room six," she murmurs, raising one eyebrow. "I already checked us in—and I stripped the bed myself. Don't make me issue a refund."

image.comp: sliding a brass room key across a counter toward him, eyebrow raised, playful smile
image.setting: inn reception desk late at night, a single lamp

3.goRes: Room six has the widest mattress in the Wayfarer, and Bettina puts every inch of it to use—losing track of the hours as you fuck her well past midnight without charging a single copper.
3.waitRes: "No refunds," she says, tucking the key into your pocket and patting your chest twice with a warm smile. "It'll keep, dear."

1.title: Clear Skies
1.text: Her grounded skyship rests on the cliff edge, timbers silvered by salt wind, the whole deck glowing copper at sunset. Rinna leads you up the gangway, tail swishing, small horns catching the amber light beneath her captain's hat. Leaning back against the rail with a salt-rough grin, she hooks a finger into your hoodie. "Sixty years flying and I never kissed anyone on deck—bad luck for sailors. Good thing we're grounded."

image.comp: on the deck of a grounded wooden skyship at sunset, wind in her hair, pulling him close by his cloak
image.setting: airship deck on a cliff edge at sunset, rigging and clouds

1.goRes: The cliff wind snaps the old canvas overhead as she kisses you hard and fast, her tail curling tightly around your ankle like a mooring rope.
1.waitRes: "Landlubber." She laughs and tosses a coil of rope at your chest, ears flattening briefly. "Next clear sunset, then—and don't jinx it."

3.title: Shore Leave
3.text: The captain's cabin door bangs open under Rinna's boot, warm lantern light spilling over chart tables and a broad, rumpled bunk. The hull creaks softly in the cliff wind as she props herself in the doorway, tossing her coat onto the floor and unbuttoning her shirt. "Shore leave," she purrs, tail lashing and coppery scales glinting in the glow. "Captain's orders—get aboard and into my bunk."

image.comp: standing in the doorway of a captain's cabin, coat thrown over her shoulder, wolfish grin
image.setting: cozy wooden captain's cabin with a hammock and charts, lamplight

3.goRes: Rinna lets out a delighted laugh, hauls you straight onto the bunk, and rides you until the old ship timbers groan in time with the headboard.
3.waitRes: "We're on a CLIFF!" She cackles, slapping the doorframe, before ruffling your hair. "Next week, then—I'll bring the rum."

2.title: The Tide Pool
2.text: The lowest pool in the Pearl Grotto glows a soft, luminous blue, the cavern walls crusted with pearls breathing light through warm steam. Maris kneels naked from the waist up at the water's edge, long ears hung with pearl drops trembling as she takes your hand and guides it beneath the surface onto her bare thigh. "Some desires are easier to speak without words," she whispers, parting her knees in the warm water.

image.comp: in a glowing tide pool in a sea cave, guiding his hand into the luminous water, half-lidded serene smile
image.setting: sea cave grotto lit by glowing pearls and luminous water

2.goRes: The pearls along the walls dim gently as your fingers slide between her slick folds beneath the glowing water, drawing soft, echoing sighs from her parted lips.
2.waitRes: "Older than your questions." She smiles softly, letting water drip from her fingers. "Come back when you're ready to stop asking—the pool will wait."

3.title: High Tide
3.text: Once a year the grotto floods to its vault with silver-blue light, the rising tide waking every pearl in the stone until the entire cavern shimmers. Maris waits completely naked on the pearl-crusted ledge, damp hair clinging to her bare breasts as warm water laps at her ankles. Her gaze is dark and steady. "Once a year," she murmurs, holding out her hand. "I have never wanted to share this with anyone—until you."

image.comp: waiting on a pearl-crusted ledge above glowing floodwater, holding out her hand to him
image.setting: flooded sea cave at high tide, glowing water and pearls everywhere

3.goRes: You join her on the warm stone ledge as the glowing tide rises around you both, sinking slowly into her heat until her breathless cries echo off the pearl-lined walls.
3.waitRes: "Next year, then." She doesn't sound disappointed—only patient as the sea itself, the pearl light soft across her bare shoulders.
